note: GROUND TRUTH. The scorers in prompts/vision_grounded.py read this file. If you regenerate the image, re-verify and update this file — a stale rubric scores a different image.

scoring_notes.people_count: Full credit for naming the correct number in any form. Partial credit scales by how close the number is (|said-expected|/expected). This is the single most discriminating check — a model that cannot count people has not understood the image.
scoring_notes.objects_present: Fraction of the three required objects the model names, each with accepted synonyms. Credit for a synonym ('cabinet' for tool chest) is deliberate: the capability is recognising the object, not matching a keyword.
scoring_notes.setting_and_activity: Half for naming the setting, half for naming a plausible activity. Both are scored on synonym lists, not exact strings.
scoring_notes.hallucination_penalty: SUBTRACTED, not awarded. Each absent-object class the model confidently asserts costs a share of the penalty. 'No dogs are visible' must NOT count as a hit — that is correct behaviour, so negation is checked before the keyword. This is the check the old char-count rubric structurally could not make: longer output was better, so inventing detail was rewarded.
